symbols.name: r
symbols.def: Fixed rank of the untreated baseline component.

symbols.name: cHi
symbols.def: Fixed upper aspect-ratio bound \(\overline c\), with \(0<\underline c<\overline c<\infty\).

symbols.name: piLo
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound \(\underline\pi\) for treated and post-period shares.

symbols.name: muLo
symbols.def: Fixed positive lower bound \(\underline\mu\) for absolute supported means.

symbols.name: muHi
symbols.def: Fixed upper bound \(\overline\mu>\underline\mu\) for absolute supported means.

symbols.name: vLo
symbols.def: Fixed positive lower bound \(\underline v\) for supported variances.

symbols.name: vHi
symbols.def: Fixed upper bound \(\overline v>\underline v\) for supported variances.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Fixed bound for the local amplitude \(\theta\).

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: Scalar limiting post-treatment share, namely the limit of \(q_T\).

symbols.name: Md
symbols.def: \(M_d=\operatorname{diag}(1-d_1,\ldots,1-d_N)\), the diagonal selector for control units.

symbols.name: Mqvec
symbols.def: \(M_{qvec}=\operatorname{diag}(1-qvec_1,\ldots,1-qvec_T)\), the diagonal selector for pre-treatment periods.

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: Common component of the treatment effect.

symbols.name: Bdom
symbols.def: Compact coefficient domain \(\mathcal B\) containing \(\gamma\) in its interior.

symbols.name: EtaLoc
symbols.type: compact subset of the nuisance space
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}=[\underline c,\overline c]\times[\underline\pi,1-\underline\pi]^2\times\bigl([ -\overline\mu,-\underline\mu]\cup[\underline\mu,\overline\mu]\bigr)\times[\underline v,\overline v]\times\bigl([ -\overline\mu,-\underline\mu]\cup[\underline\mu,\overline\mu]\bigr)\times[\underline v,\overline v]\), in the coordinate order of \(\eta\).

symbols.name: sone
symbols.def: \(s_1(B)\) is the largest singular value of \(B\).

symbols.name: Gstab
symbols.def: \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{stab}}=\{(\eta,h):\mathcal S(\eta,h)=\{x_0\}\text{ for some }x_0,\ \inf_{|x-x_0|\ge\epsilon}[\Phi_{\eta,h}(x)-\Phi_{\eta,h}(x_0)]>0\text{ for every }\epsilon>0\}\).

symbols.name: xstar
symbols.def: \(x_\star(\eta,h)\) is the unique member of \(\mathcal S(\eta,h)\) on \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{stab}}\).

symbols.name: betaHatF
symbols.def: \(\widehat\beta_F=\min\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathcal B}Q_F(\beta)\); the smallest-real-number rule is the measurable coefficient selection.

symbols.name: LhatF
symbols.def: \(\widehat L_F\) is the row-major lexicographically smallest matrix among best rank-\(r+1\) approximations to \(Y-\widehat\beta_FD\).

symbols.name: Uhat
symbols.def: \(\widehat U\) is the column space of \(\widehat L_F\), completed to dimension \(r+1\), if needed, by the first linearly independent standard basis vectors under lexicographic Gram--Schmidt.

symbols.name: Vhat
symbols.def: \(\widehat V\) is the row space of \(\widehat L_F\), completed to dimension \(r+1\), if needed, by the first linearly independent standard basis vectors under lexicographic Gram--Schmidt.

symbols.name: sigmaHatF
symbols.def:
For \(
u_F>0\), \(\widehat\sigma_F=[
u_F^{-1}\|Y-\widehat eta_FD-\widehat L_F\|_F^2]^{1/2}\), using the nonnegative root; set \(\widehat\sigma_F=0\) for \(
u_F\le0\).

symbols.name: CA
symbols.def: Fixed loading-radius constant \(C_A\) in the masked fitting class.

symbols.name: CB
symbols.def: Fixed factor-radius constant \(C_B\) in the masked fitting class.

symbols.name: LhatM
symbols.def: \(\widehat L_M\) is the row-major lexicographically smallest fitted matrix \(AB^{\top}\) among global minimizers of \(\sum_{(i,t)\in\Omega_0}(Y_{it}-A_i^{\top}B_t)^2\), subject to \(B^{\top}B/T=I_r\), \(\max_i\|A_i\|_2\le C_A\), and \(\max_t\|B_t\|_2\le C_B\).

symbols.name: sigmaHatM
symbols.def:
For \(
u_M>0\), \(\widehat\sigma_M=[
u_M^{-1}\sum_{(i,t)\in\Omega_0}(Y_{it}-\widehat L_{M,it})^2]^{1/2}\), using the nonnegative root; set \(\widehat\sigma_M=0\) for \(
u_M\le0\).

novel.justification: This paper maintains a deterministic uniform strong-loading envelope, satisfied by fixed-rank panels whose empirical loading Gram matrices remain in a compact positive-definite set.
This paper maintains a deterministic uniform strong-factor envelope, satisfied by fixed-rank common-state arrays with uniformly nondegenerate empirical covariance.
This paper maintains a deterministic incoherence envelope, satisfied by stratified panels with uniformly bounded baseline characteristics and fixed factor rank.
This paper maintains a deterministic factor-row envelope, satisfied when common shocks range over a compact state space and factor rank is fixed.
Stable treated-unit score moments arise when a fixed population share is treated and the empirical exposure distribution stabilizes.
Stable post-period score moments arise in deterministic finite-support triangular arrays whose empirical state frequencies converge.
The compact geometry collects nondegenerate treated shares, signed nonzero average responses, and bounded response dispersion while allowing both treatment-effect directions.
Every panel retains genuine treated-unit and post-period response dispersion, as in stratified exposure panels with stable cell shares.
This paper maintains bounded unit-side scores, satisfied by normalized exposure intensities or finitely supported dose strata.
This paper maintains bounded time-side scores, satisfied by normalized event-time responses or finitely supported aggregate states.

This restriction defines the exact-oracle array class and is jointly feasible in balanced finite-cell arrays with signed loading contrasts. Its sole mathematical role is to annihilate baseline-factor cross terms with the treatment support, thereby isolating fitted-singular-direction absorption from ordinary baseline confounding; it neither describes an observable construction nor selects a profile minimizer.

This restriction defines the exact-oracle array class and is jointly feasible when repeated finite cells provide loading contrasts orthogonal to both the treatment indicator and the supported score. Its sole mathematical role is to annihilate baseline-factor cross terms with the heterogeneous left score; it neither describes an observable construction nor selects a profile minimizer.

This restriction defines the exact-oracle array class and is jointly feasible in balanced finite-cell arrays with signed factor contrasts. Its sole mathematical role is to annihilate baseline-factor cross terms with the post-period support, thereby isolating fitted-singular-direction absorption from ordinary baseline confounding; it neither describes an observable construction nor selects a profile minimizer.

This restriction defines the exact-oracle array class and is jointly feasible when repeated finite cells provide factor contrasts orthogonal to both the post-period indicator and the supported score. Its sole mathematical role is to annihilate baseline-factor cross terms with the heterogeneous right score; it neither describes an observable construction nor selects a profile minimizer.
This paper maintains a deterministic restricted-Gram envelope for control-unit loadings, satisfied when every latent direction has a uniformly positive control share.
This paper maintains a deterministic restricted-Gram envelope for pre-period factors, satisfied when every latent direction has a uniformly positive pre-period share.
The masked loading radius is fixed above the normalized-baseline envelope; compact loading designs permit such nonrandom slack.
The masked factor radius is fixed above the normalized-baseline envelope; bounded common-state panels permit such nonrandom slack.
A bounded contiguous-amplitude experiment captures systematic heterogeneity comparable to the rectangular noise edge while allowing both signs.
A bounded parameterization of the common effect permits a compact coefficient domain with fixed interior slack, excluding boundary selection artifacts from the abstract limit experiment.

definitions.name: Measurable full-sample rank profile
definitions.construction: \(Q_F(\beta)=\|Y-\beta D\|_F^2-\sum_{j=1}^{r+1}s_j(Y-\beta D)^2\) and \(\widehat\beta_F=\min\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathcal B}Q_F(\beta)\). After this scalar selection, \(\widehat L_F\) is the row-major lexicographically smallest best rank-\(r+1\) approximation; \(\widehat U\) and \(\widehat V\) use the stated lexicographic completion rule.

definitions.name: Global-selection algebraic handle
definitions.construction: Rotate signs so that \(B_{\eta,h}(x)=\begin{pmatrix}z&b_0\\c_0&d_0\end{pmatrix}\) with \(b_0,c_0,d_0>0\); combine \(t+u=z^2+b_0^2+c_0^2+d_0^2\), \(tu=(zd_0-b_0c_0)^2\), and \(z(t-u)=(1-c/t^2)\{z(t-d_0^2)+d_0b_0c_0\}\), then compare all stationary branches, spectral-edge junctions, and tails. At a separated tie, augment this branch comparison with the coefficient-indexed Gaussian singular-value process and the complete local nuisance-drift path.

definitions.name: Conventional residualized IFE Wald interval
definitions.construction:
Use the selected \(\widehat L_F\), \(\widehat U\), and \(\widehat V\). Set \(
u_F=NT-1-(r+1)(N+T-r-1)\); for \(
u_F>0\), use the nonnegative root \(\widehat\sigma_F=[
u_F^{-1}\|Y-\widehat eta_FD-\widehat L_F\|_F^2]^{1/2}\), and set it to zero otherwise. Form \(\widetilde D=(I_N-P_{\widehat U})D(I_T-P_{\widehat V})\). Return \(\mathrm{CI}_F=[\widehat eta_F\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_F/\|\widetilde D\|_F]\) when \(\|\widetilde D\|_F>0\), and \(\mathbb R\) otherwise.

definitions.name: Rank-\(r\) masked-cell benchmark statistic
definitions.construction: Choose the row-major lexicographically smallest fitted matrix \(\widehat L_M=AB^{\top}\) among minimizers of \(\sum_{(i,t)\in\Omega_0}(Y_{it}-A_i^{\top}B_t)^2\) under \(B^{\top}B/T=I_r\), \(\max_i\|A_i\|_2\le C_A\), and \(\max_t\|B_t\|_2\le C_B\). Then set \(\widehat{\operatorname{ATT}}_M=(n_1t_1)^{-1}\sum_{i:d_i=1}\sum_{t:qvec_t=1}(Y_{it}-\widehat L_{M,it})\).

definitions.name: Masked studentized interval
definitions.construction:
Set \(
u_M=|\Omega_0|-r(N+T-r)=NT-n_1t_1-r(N+T-r)\). For \(
u_M>0\), use the nonnegative root \(\widehat\sigma_M=[
u_M^{-1}\sum_{(i,t)\in\Omega_0}(Y_{it}-\widehat L_{M,it})^2]^{1/2}\), and set it to zero otherwise. Return \(\mathrm{CI}_M=[\widehat{\operatorname{ATT}}_M\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_M/\sqrt{n_1t_1}]\).

statements.statement: For every fixed \(r\) and every \(c\in[\underline c,\overline c]\), there exist dimensions \(N,T\to\infty\) and deterministic arrays \(d,qvec,a,b,\Lambda,F\) such that \(c_N\to c\), \(\eta_{NT}\to\eta\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}})\), \(\Lambda^{\top}d=\Lambda^{\top}a_S=0\), \(F^{\top}qvec=F^{\top}b_S=0\), the full Gram limits \(N^{-1}\Lambda^{\top}\Lambda\) and \(T^{-1}F^{\top}F\) are positive definite, the selector-restricted limits \(N^{-1}\Lambda^{\top}M_d\Lambda\) and \(T^{-1}F^{\top}M_{qvec}F\) are positive definite, and the loading, factor, and treatment-score rows are uniformly bounded. Hence the exact-oracle triangular-array class is nonempty without imposing any rule for selecting a minimizer of \(\Phi_{\eta,h}\).
statements.justification: The sensitivity experiment must contain concrete deterministic sequences rather than rely on mutually inconsistent oracle restrictions.
statements.gap: This is a nonvacuity certificate for the paper's abstract class, not a claim that the restrictions are observable or operationally constructible.
statements.consumer: It validates that the absorption phase law is evaluated on a nonempty confounding-free oracle class.

statements.statement: For nuisance sequences with \(\eta_{NT}\to\eta\), uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\) and every finite \(M\), \(\sup_{|x|\le M}|(\sigma^2T)^{-1}[Q_F(\gamma+\sigma x/\sqrt m)-Q_F(\gamma)]-[\Phi_{NT,h}(x)-\Phi_{NT,h}(0)]|\xrightarrow{p}0\). Moreover, \(\widehat x_F=O_p(1)\) uniformly and \(\operatorname{dist}\{\widehat x_F,\mathcal S_{NT}(h)\}\xrightarrow{p}0\). Here \(h=\theta/\sigma\in[-\overline h,\overline h]\); no stochastic assertion is made for unbounded \(h\) or a genuine limiting tie.
statements.justification: This is the bridge from fixed-spike random-matrix theory to the coefficient chosen by the actual full-sample IFE objective on a bounded local experiment.
statements.gap: Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi (2012) give fixed-spike limits; Bai (2009) does not cover a noise-scale treatment factor or uniform coefficient-indexed spectral localization.
statements.consumer: It supplies the limit experiment needed to determine whether whole-sample profiling can absorb local low-rank heterogeneity even after ordinary baseline-confounding terms are removed by assumption.

statements.statement: Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\) satisfying \(\kappa^2h^2(\mu_a^2v_b+v_a\mu_b^2+v_av_b)<\sqrt c\), \(\mathcal S(\eta,h)=\{x_{\operatorname{ATT}}\}\) and \(\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})/\sigma\xrightarrow{p}0\).
statements.justification: The result certifies a nonempty positive-signal region in which fitting the extra factor is harmless at the local ATT scale.
statements.gap: Cardoso, Ferman, and Fernandes (2026) analyze an asymptotically strong heterogeneous factor and do not contain a bounded subcritical no-absorption region.
statements.consumer: It identifies the harmless side of the theoretical absorption frontier within the exact-oracle class.

statements.statement: Classify \(\mathcal S(\eta,h)\) outside the stable-singleton restriction. Either establish uniqueness and separation, or enumerate every genuine separated tie and derive a measurable next-order selection functional of the complete nuisance-drift path and the coefficient-indexed limiting noise process. The classification must include opposite admissible \(m^{-1/4}\) drifts toward a tie.
statements.justification: Global selection is the irreducible open content because deterministic uniform convergence cannot choose between separated equal minima.
statements.gap: Neither coefficient profiling nor spiked-matrix edge theory supplies a measurable selector at a drift-sensitive tie of this endogenous scalar potential.
statements.consumer: The answer determines whether the abstract full-sample coefficient has a stable limit at every detectability boundary.

statements.statement: Uniformly over every compact subset of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\), \(\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})/\sigma\xrightarrow{p}x_\star(\eta,h)-h\mu_a\mu_b\). There is a nonempty relatively open subset of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\) on which \(x_\star(\eta,h)\ne h\mu_a\mu_b\). No assertion is made at a genuine tie or for \(|h|>\overline h\).
statements.justification: This theorem is the explicit local ATT-absorption phase law on the bounded stochastic experiment.
statements.gap: Cardoso, Ferman, and Fernandes (2026) give a strong-signal endpoint; the stable-singleton bounded local transition map is absent.
statements.consumer: The law is the primary sensitivity result: whole-sample profiling can absorb bounded local low-rank heterogeneity in a confounding-free oracle class.

statements.statement: Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\). Along any deterministic branch with \((\eta,h)\in\mathcal G_{\mathrm{stab}}\) for all sufficiently large \(|h|\), \(x_\star(\eta,h)=c\mu_a\mu_b\{\kappa^4v_av_b(\mu_a^2+v_a)(\mu_b^2+v_b)\}^{-1}h^{-3}+o(h^{-3})\) as \(|h|\to\infty\), and hence \(x_\star(\eta,h)\to0\). This is a calculation for the deterministic profile and is not a stochastic triangular-array limit under \(\theta\in[-K,K]\).
statements.justification: Separating the deterministic endpoint records how the profile approaches complete absorption without mixing an unbounded signal with the bounded local experiment.
statements.gap: The strong-factor endpoint in Cardoso, Ferman, and Fernandes (2026) does not provide this deterministic profile expansion.
statements.consumer: The endpoint checks that the bounded-local profile has the correct deterministic connection to complete absorption.

statements.statement: There is a nonempty relatively open subset \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{abs}}\subset\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\) of the absorbed region on which \(\|\widetilde D\|_F/\sqrt{NT}\to a_D>0\), \(\widehat\sigma_F\xrightarrow{p}\sigma\), and \(\Pr\{\operatorname{ATT}_{NT}\in\mathrm{CI}_F\}\to0\). Thus coverage is strictly below \(1-\alpha\) on \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{abs}}\), only for bounded \(h=\theta/\sigma\).
statements.justification: A selected-factor bias of order \(m^{-1/2}\) dominates the conventional interval width of order \(m^{-1}\).
statements.gap: Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026) establish possible weak-factor distortion but not this explicit bounded-local low-rank-treatment zero-coverage region.
statements.consumer: The result converts the absorption phase into a formal sensitivity failure for conventional whole-sample Wald inference within the oracle class.

statements.statement: For all sufficiently large \(N,T\), \(G_F\succ0\), and \(\Lambda F^{\top}=(\Lambda G_F^{1/2})(FG_F^{-1/2})^{\top}\) satisfies \(T^{-1}(FG_F^{-1/2})^{\top}(FG_F^{-1/2})=I_r\), \(\max_i\|(\Lambda G_F^{1/2})_{i\cdot}\|_2<C_A\), and \(\max_t\|(FG_F^{-1/2})_{t\cdot}\|_2<C_B\). Hence the true baseline factorization belongs to the masked fitting class.
statements.justification: The normalization and radii must contain the data-generating baseline rather than merely define a compact optimization domain.
statements.gap: Bai and Ng (2021) normalize factors for tall-wide rotation, but feasibility under these explicit deterministic radii must be recorded.
statements.consumer: The lemma validates the optimization domain of the internal masked benchmark before its coverage theorem is invoked.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(\theta\in[-K,K]\), \(\sqrt{n_1t_1}(\widehat{\operatorname{ATT}}_M-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})/\widehat\sigma_M\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\), \(\widehat\sigma_M\xrightarrow{p}\sigma\), and \(\inf_{\theta\in[-K,K]}\Pr\{\operatorname{ATT}_{NT}\in\mathrm{CI}_M\}\to1-\alpha\). In addition, \((n_1t_1)^{-1}\sum_{i:d_i=1}\sum_{t:qvec_t=1}\widehat L_{M,it}=o_p((n_1t_1)^{-1/2})\) uniformly.
statements.justification: As an internal control, masking removes the heterogeneous treatment factor from every training cell, so uniformity spans the bounded absorption transition.
statements.gap: Bai and Ng (2021) give pointwise block-imputation normality, not this compact-amplitude result paired with full-sample absorption.
statements.consumer: It supplies an internal benchmark showing that the full-sample failure is caused by fitting the treated-post spike rather than by the Gaussian oracle experiment itself.

statements.justification: This sanity reduction prevents spurious absorption bias when heterogeneous treatment variation is absent.
statements.gap: Bai (2009) supplies the homogeneous-effect benchmark but not its embedding as the zero-signal point of a local profile.
statements.consumer: The theoretical sensitivity map reduces to the familiar homogeneous-effect benchmark at zero amplitude.

sampling_model.design: Abstract triangular rectangular fixed-design panel with \(N/T\to c\in(0,\infty)\) and one deterministic treated-post block.
sampling_model.units: The arrays \(d,qvec,a,b,\Lambda,F\) are fixed members of the exact-oracle class defined by the four stated orthogonality restrictions; those restrictions remove baseline-factor cross terms but do not select a profile minimizer. Randomness comes only from iid Gaussian \(E_{it}\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(D=dqvec^{\top}\), with heterogeneous treated-post component \(\theta(d\odot a)(qvec\odot b)^{\top}/\sqrt m\).
sampling_model.overlap: The scalar shares \(p_N\) and \(q_T\) have interior limits \(p\) and \(q\). The restricted Grams use the diagonal control selector \(M_d\) and diagonal pre-period selector \(M_{qvec}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Full-sample IFE profiles rank \(r+1\) with smallest-coefficient, lexicographic best-approximation, and lexicographic subspace-completion rules. The internal masked benchmark fits rank \(r\) only on \(D_{it}=0\), with radii containing the normalized true baseline. Both intervals use their stated residual degrees of freedom and nonnegative-root conventions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The profiled IFE coefficient is consistent and asymptotically normal under strong-factor and identification conditions.
The slope limit distribution is invariant to fitting more factors than the true rank under the paper's regularity conditions.
A fixed rectangular finite-rank perturbation separates from the noise edge exactly above the \(D\)-transform threshold.
Bias-aware intervals attain uniform coverage over factor strength under generalized regressor non-collinearity.
With an asymptotically strong treatment-effect factor, full-sample IFE converges to the common component \(\gamma\) rather than ATT.
Tall-wide factor imputation yields pointwise asymptotic normality for an ATT estimator under strong observed-block factor conditions.
IFE with a growing fitted factor count converges to a conditional-variance-weighted average of heterogeneous treatment effects.
Potential-factor models identify systematic causal effects and provide feasible counterfactual inference using untreated or treatment-specific factor structure.

tldr: This paper studies an abstract exact-oracle panel limit experiment in which four finite-array orthogonality restrictions remove ordinary baseline-confounding terms without determining the profiled coefficient. Whole-sample IFE can then absorb a bounded local heterogeneous treatment effect when its rectangular spike becomes detectable. The paper derives the coefficient-indexed two-by-two profile, proves the absorption law on compact stable-singleton geometries, maps an absorbed region into conventional-Wald undercoverage, and uses masked fitting only as an internal benchmark control. The large-signal endpoint is solely a deterministic profile calculation, and selection at genuine ties remains open.

project_justification.gap: Existing panel theory covers regular strong factors, generic weak-factor robustness, or the strong bad-control endpoint, while random-matrix theory fixes the spike before taking limits. None controls a bounded coefficient-indexed treatment spike in the global IFE criterion after ordinary baseline-confounding terms have been removed by defining restrictions.
project_justification.niche: An exact-oracle noise-scale treatment factor creates a nonregular sensitivity experiment connecting harmless over-fitting to ATT absorption.
project_justification.fill: The project derives \(\Phi_{\eta,h}\), proves bounded-local profile convergence and the absorption map on stable-singleton geometries, isolates tie selection as an open question, derives conventional-Wald failure, and uses masked fitting only as an internal control within the same abstract experiment.

related_work: Bai (2009) supplies the moment and limiting Gram framework for regular profiled IFE; the deterministic Gram envelopes, maximum-row bounds, and treatment-score bounds here are this paper's own sufficient regularity conditions. Moon and Weidner (2015) show harmless rank overestimation under a class excluding low-rank regressors. Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi (2012) supply fixed-spike rectangular outlier maps, while Bloemendal and Virag (2013) describe near-critical edge laws. Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026) inform the weak-factor inference question but exclude the rank-one block treatment through non-collinearity. Cardoso, Ferman, and Fernandes (2026) establish the strong treatment-factor bad-control endpoint, not the bounded local path. Juodis and Weidner (2026) characterize variance-weighted limits under growing fitted rank. Bai and Ng (2021) inform tall-wide imputation, restricted observed-block Gram conditions, and pointwise ATT theory; masked fitting here is only an internal control using the actual diagonal control and pre-period selectors and explicit normalization, radius, and residual-degrees-of-freedom conventions. Bai and Wang (2026) organize causal effects through potential factor structures rather than a whole-sample absorption profile. Gobillon and Magnac (2016) motivate studying whole-sample and counterfactual factor fits; the exact-oracle theorem has no direct operational implication for their empirical setting.
technical_internal_limitation: The four exact orthogonality restrictions define the admissible triangular-array class. They remove baseline-factor cross terms so that coefficient distortion isolates absorption by the fitted singular direction, but they do not select a minimizer of the profile. Masking is not itself the novelty and says nothing about ordinary baseline-confounding bias outside this class. If separated minima admit opposite \(m^{-1/4}\) nuisance drifts with identical limiting coordinates but different selections, no selector indexed only by \((\eta,h)\) is valid. The stochastic theorems therefore stop at bounded stable-singleton geometries.
honest_scope: The proposal is an abstract exact-oracle sensitivity benchmark. The stochastic profile, selection, absorption, and Wald claims concern only \(\theta\in[-K,K]\), \(h\in[-\overline h,\overline h]\), and compact stable-singleton geometries. The limit \(|h|\to\infty\) belongs solely to a deterministic profile proposition. Complete global minimizer classification and drift-sensitive tie selection remain open. Exact finite-array orthogonality is a defining restriction, not an observable residualization procedure, and it does not encode which profile minimizer is selected. Masked fitting is only an internal control; neither it nor the oracle class is claimed as a new practical estimator. At \(\theta=0\), the profile reduces to the homogeneous-effect benchmark.

seed_details.question: Can masked imputation remain uniformly studentized over bounded local heterogeneity while full-sample IFE absorbs?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Make the aggregate imputation remainder uniform in the local amplitude and compare both procedures on one triangular array.
seed_details.destination_search: The carried search found pointwise imputation theory but no joint uniform divergence theorem.
seed_details.referee_objection: Block-imputation ATT normality is already known.
seed_details.rebuttal: The published theorem is pointwise and is not paired with a local full-sample absorption transition.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Theorem 1.5 was read for near-critical stochastic-operator limits.
seed_details.question: Is there a drift-indexed selection law at a genuine profile tie?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Couple the coefficient-indexed perturbation with the edge process and the full nuisance-drift path.
seed_details.destination_search: The carried search found no regression-indexed rectangular argmin law.
seed_details.referee_objection: Edge fluctuations vanish at first order away from ties.
seed_details.rebuttal: The question is retained only for genuine ties and finer drift.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The general-noise hypotheses and universality boundaries were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.question: Is the coefficient-indexed absorption profile universal beyond Gaussian noise?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Replace rotation invariance by a uniform anisotropic local law.
seed_details.destination_search: The carried search found fixed-spike universality but not a profiled argmin.
seed_details.rebuttal: Continuum-indexed argmin uniformity is not routine but is outside the first paper.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The minimax-linear program, error bound, coverage theorem, and low-rank-regressor exclusion were read.
seed_details.question: Can bias-aware inference be redesigned for an exactly low-rank treatment regressor?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Replace the zero non-collinearity criterion by a different target decomposition.
seed_details.destination_search: The carried search found no bias-aware ATT interval at this scale.
seed_details.rebuttal: Observed blocks and oracle orthogonality identify ATT here, but masking is more direct.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The factor-versus-synthetic-control comparison was read from the public discussion paper as motivation for studying alternative fitting samples; the exact-oracle theorem has no direct operational implication for that empirical design.
seed_details.question: Does staggered adoption yield a finite matrix-valued absorption profile?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Replace the rank-one block by interacting cohort spikes and a vector coefficient profile.
seed_details.destination_search: The carried search found no coefficient-indexed finite-rank spike analysis.
seed_details.rebuttal: Crossing cohort spikes create a vector argmin, but the extension is premature.

literature_map.settled: Profile least squares is regular under strong factors and non-collinear regressors; rank overestimation is harmless in that class.
literature_map.unsettled: The class excludes a low-rank treatment regressor whose local factor changes with the profiled coefficient.

literature_map.settled: Fixed spikes have explicit outlier and overlap limits, and near-critical eigenvalues have edge laws.
literature_map.unsettled: No cited result gives global argmin selection for a coefficient-indexed spike path.

literature_map.settled: Strong treatment factors may be absorbed, and broad heterogeneous-panel slopes may be variance weighted.
literature_map.unsettled: Neither result derives the bounded local transition or its conventional-Wald law.

literature_map.settled: Observed-block factor and matrix-completion methods avoid fitting treated post-treatment outcomes.
literature_map.unsettled: No adjacent result proves uniform studentization on the same bounded sequence on which full-sample IFE changes branch.

literature_map.settled: The cited study motivates comparing whole-sample IFE with counterfactual and synthetic-control estimators.
literature_map.unsettled: The exact-oracle theorem has no direct operational implication for that empirical design.

literature_map.settled: Large-factor and potential-factor frameworks organize estimation and systematic causal effects.
literature_map.unsettled: They do not analyze a local treatment-supported factor competing for an additional singular direction.

literature_checklist.author: Bai

literature_checklist.one_line: Shows harmless rank overestimation while excluding low-rank regressors.

literature_checklist.author: Cardoso, Ferman, and Fernandes
literature_checklist.one_line: Proves complete absorption when treatment heterogeneity is asymptotically strong.

literature_checklist.author: Bai and Ng
literature_checklist.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
literature_checklist.one_line: Uses tall-wide rotation for counterfactual imputation and pointwise ATT theory.

literature_checklist.author: Juodis and Weidner

literature_checklist.author: Gobillon and Magnac
